p.n: The Rat Points Out Their Common Problem

body.p:

You, too: no one is more capable of helping you get out of this plight than I am.

You will know the truth of my words and that they bear no lie
or deceit. You can see where the mongoose is, lying in ambush for me, and where the owl is, wanting
to snatch me, and both are my enemies. They, however, fear and avoid you.
If you safeguard me and vow not to kill me, I shall approach you and cut your cords, delivering you from that in which you are and saving myself in the act. Be reassured as to
what I have mentioned,
and trust me through it.

For no one is farther from the good than two whose situation is the same and their quality
is different: one, is he who trusts no one; and the other, is he whom
no one trusts.

I will fulfill to you the commitment I pledged on my behalf. So do accept
this from me and be open to me. Don’t delay the matter while you can

p.n: The Intelligent Does Not Postpone Action

body.p:
The sensible man does not
postpone his action beyond its time.

p.n: The Cat Should Desire Common Rescue

body.p:
And let yourself be pleased by my survival as I will be pleased
by yours, for either one of us shall indeed be saved by the other- as with

p.n: Sailors Depend on Ships and Vice Versa

body.p:
a ship at sea: it survives
with the help of the passengers and the passengers survive with the help of the ship.

So, through cooperating-you and I-can we hope
for survival from this trouble.’”

p.n: The Cat Puts His Trust in the Rat

body.p:
“When the cat heard the rat’s speech, he knew
that he was truthful; so he got delighted by them, believing his words, and said to the rat, ‘I see that these words
of yours are akin to truth and sincerity I accept this truce, in which for myself and you, I hope, will be deliverance.
